# Kathy Watanabe
“I welcome the opportunity to once again serve our City and provide proven leadership focused on strengthening Santa Clara’s economic growth, enhancing quality of life, expanding leadership opportunities for our youth, and maintaining a strong commitment to public safety, environmental stewardship, and long-term sustainability.”
## Thank you to everyone who attended our kickoff event!
## Kathy Watanabe for Mayor of Santa Clara
### Proven Leadership.
###### Why i’m running for mayor
## When I termed off the Santa Clara City Council in 2024, I was proud to have served all residents of our City for eight years. Public service has been one of the greatest honors of my life.
Yet time moves quickly, and there were still important goals and priorities I wanted to achieve for our community.
When members of the public and business community approached me about running for Mayor, it reaffirmed that people saw in me a leader with the experience, commitment, and vision to continue serving Santa Clara.
I welcome the opportunity to once again serve our City and provide proven leadership focused on strengthening Santa Clara’s economic growth, enhancing quality of life, expanding leadership opportunities for our youth, and maintaining a strong commitment to public safety, environmental stewardship, and long-term sustainability.
###### Priority Issues
#### There are many issues facing our community, but I have identified several key priorities that I believe require immediate attention.
###### 01
##### Fiscal Responsibility and Smart Growth
“Protect taxpayer dollars while planning for Santa Clara’s future.”
Focus on transparent budgeting, maintaining reserves, evaluating major projects carefully, and ensuring development pays for needed infrastructure and city services. Voters often respond to the idea that growth should benefit residents rather than create new burdens.
###### 02
##### Public Safety and Emergency Preparedness
“Keep neighborhoods safe and ensure our city is prepared.”
Include police, fire, traffic safety, disaster readiness, wildfire preparedness, and neighborhood quality-of-life concerns. Public safety consistently ranks among top local priorities.
###### 03
##### Housing Solutions That Protect Community Character
“Create balanced housing solutions that work for residents.”
Emphasize practical approaches: workforce housing, senior housing options, responsible planning, and preserving neighborhoods while complying with state requirements.
###### 04
##### Strong Neighborhoods and Quality of Life
“Invest in the services residents use every day.”
This can include parks, libraries, streets, traffic congestion relief, beautification, recreation programs, and community gathering spaces. People often vote based on the daily experience of living in their city.
###### 05
##### Economic Opportunity and Local Partnerships
“Support businesses and create a strong local economy.”
Highlight attracting quality jobs, supporting small businesses, partnering with major employers, and keeping Santa Clara economically competitive while preserving local identity.
###### 06
##### Bringing Back Leadership Programs
“Support opportunities that help students and residents succeed.”
Covid-19 impacted Santa Clara's leadership programs (i.e., Leadership Santa Clara and Citizens Police Academy). Those programs helped develop great City leaders and need to be brought back.
###### Vision & Beliefs
### It’s time to bring proven leadership back to City Hall!
- Equality, justice and compassion
- Accountability and fiscal responsibility
- Integrity, honesty and trustworthiness
- Innovation, progress and sustainability
###### Experience
## About Kathy
Kathy Watanabe has proudly called Santa Clara home since 2005. She and her husband, Karl, have been married since 2000 and are raising their daughter, Kayleigh, in the community they love.
A dedicated community volunteer and advocate, Kathy served on the first Parent-Teacher Organization at Don Callejon School from 2006 to 2008. She played a key role in advocating for the Northside Library, working alongside local and state leaders to help bring the project to fruition and celebrate its opening in 2014. Kathy also worked with community members, elected officials, and educational leaders to support Santa Clara Unified School District’s acquisition of land in North San José for the development of a new school campus.
Before serving on the City Council, Kathy dedicated eight years to the City of Santa Clara Library Board of Trustees and served three years as President of Santa Clara Sister Cities. During her tenure, she helped finalize the Sister City partnership between Santa Clara and Limerick, strengthening international relationships and cultural exchange opportunities for residents.
In March 2016, Kathy was appointed to the Santa Clara City Council representing Seat 6 and was subsequently elected by voters in November 2016, receiving 48% of the vote in a citywide at-large election and carrying every precinct in the city. In December 2017, her colleagues unanimously selected her to serve as Vice Mayor for 2018.
During Kathy’s first term on the City Council, she was a strong advocate for Northside residents impacted by NFL games and major events at Levi’s Stadium. She worked tirelessly to ensure that neighborhood concerns regarding traffic, parking, noise, and quality-of-life issues were heard and addressed.
In 2020, Kathy sought re-election in the newly created District 1 and faced an unprecedented challenge. Political Action Committees funded by Jed York spent nearly $1 million in an effort to defeat her campaign. Despite being vastly outspent, Kathy earned the trust and support of District 1 voters and was re-elected to the City Council. Demonstrating the strength of her grassroots support, she won decisively again, reaffirming her reputation as an independent leader who puts residents first.
During her eight years on the City Council, Kathy championed economic development, neighborhood services, public safety, environmental sustainability, and community engagement. She served on numerous regional and local committees, including the Cities Association of Santa Clara County, the San José/Santa Clara Treatment Plant Advisory Committee and the Northern California Power Agency.
Prior to her public service, Kathy spent 40 years in the legal profession, working for several prestigious law firms in both New York and California. Her legal background provided the foundation for her commitment to transparency, accountability, and effective governance.
In November 2024, Kathy was elected to the Governing Board of the Santa Clara Unified School District, earning nearly 80% of the vote in Trustee Area 2. She was sworn into office on December 19, 2024, continuing her long-standing commitment to serving Santa Clara’s students, families, and residents.
Today, Kathy remains focused on strengthening Santa Clara’s neighborhoods, supporting educational excellence, promoting economic vitality, and ensuring a high quality of life for future generations.
